name: Anterolateral hip approach (Watson-Jones)
corridor: Interval between tensor fasciae latae anteriorly and gluteus medius posteriorly

positioning.text: Position supine or lateral according to the planned procedure, with the greater trochanter and anterior superior iliac spine accessible.

setup.text: Drape to permit hip motion and distal extension along the lateral femur when fixation is planned.

surface_landmarks.text: Mark the anterior superior iliac spine, greater trochanter, and femoral shaft.

incision.text: Center the incision over the anterolateral greater trochanter, extending proximally toward the anterior superior iliac spine and distally along the femur as needed.

superficial_interval.text: Open fascia lata and develop the interval between tensor fasciae latae anteriorly and gluteus medius posteriorly.

deep_interval.text: Expose the anterior capsule while protecting the abductors; limited release of anterior vastus lateralis or abductor insertion may be required by the procedure.

layers.text: Skin, subcutaneous tissue, fascia lata, tensor–gluteus medius interval, pericapsular tissue, then anterior hip capsule.

structures_encountered.text: Branches of the lateral femoral circumflex system may cross the interval and should be controlled deliberately.

structures_at_risk.text: The superior gluteal nerve and vessels limit proximal dissection, and femoral neurovascular structures are at risk from anterior retractor placement.

danger_zones.text: Do not extend the gluteus medius dissection proximally without accounting for the superior gluteal neurovascular bundle.

retraction_hazards.text: Keep anterior retractors on bone and avoid deep medial placement toward the femoral nerve and vessels.

exposure.text: Provides access to the anterior hip capsule, acetabular rim, femoral neck, and lateral proximal femur.

limitations.text: Posterior acetabular access is limited, and aggressive abductor release can compromise postoperative abductor function.

extensions.text: Extend distally by elevating the anterior vastus lateralis to accommodate lateral proximal-femoral implants.

indications.text: Applicable to total hip arthroplasty, hemiarthroplasty, selected femoral-neck fracture procedures, and proximal-femoral exposure.

relative_contraindications.text: Consider another exposure when extensive posterior acetabular visualization or a broader femoral corridor is required.

implant_implications.text: Lateral plate or sliding-hip-screw application may require distal extension and anterior elevation of vastus lateralis.

fluoroscopy_implications.text: Choose table and positioning to preserve AP and lateral imaging before draping, especially when fracture fixation is planned.

closure.text: Repair the capsule and any released abductor or vastus lateralis attachment, then close fascia lata securely.

complications.text: Approach-related complications include abductor weakness or limp, femoral neurovascular injury from retraction, vascular bleeding, and iatrogenic femoral fracture during exposure.

bailouts.text: When visualization or femoral mobilization is inadequate, extend the defined exposure rather than applying uncontrolled retraction; convert to the procedure's planned extensile option when necessary.

procedure_applications.condition: Open reduction and lateral proximal-femoral fixation are required

questions.question: What muscular interval defines the Watson-Jones approach?
questions.answer: Tensor fasciae latae anteriorly and gluteus medius posteriorly.

questions.question: What structure limits proximal extension of this approach?
